images.title: The division ladder for the HCF
images.purpose: Show the common division steps for 84 and 180 and that the divisors on the left multiply to the HCF.
images.composition: One ladder in the centre left with four rows, the divisors in a column on its left, and one result line to the right, with wide margins.
exact_structure: Row 1: 84 and 180 side by side. Row 2: 42 and 90. Row 3: 21 and 45. Row 4: 7 and 15. Exactly 4 rows, 8 numbers, all in teal #0072B2 except row 4 in amber #E69F00.
Exactly 3 divisors in a column to the left of rows 1 to 3, top to bottom: 2, 2, 3, each in a reddish purple #CC79A7 circle.
Thin grey #6B7280 L shaped division bars: one vertical bar right of the divisor column and one horizontal line under each of rows 1 to 3.
A reddish purple bracket groups the 3 circled divisors and points right to one bold line: HCF = 2 × 2 × 3 = 12.
rejection: any row that is not the row above divided by its divisor
an HCF other than 12, or divisors other than 2, 2, 3 in that order
more or fewer than 4 rows or 3 circled divisors
images.takeaway: Divide both numbers by common primes until none is left; the divisors multiply to the HCF.
images.description: A division ladder 84, 180 to 42, 90 to 21, 45 to 7, 15 with divisors 2, 2, 3 circled and HCF = 12.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video on reading the common division method.
images.teaching_notes: Read each row down from the one above, then read only the circled divisors for the HCF.

image_decisions.why: The ladder is a layout students must read row by row, so a clean picture of it is the core of this concept.
